name: Fenra Cloudberry-Hibiscus Tonic
description: A premium tonic-style soda using real Nordic cloudberry extract blended with hibiscus concentrate, lightly bitter, designed as a mixer but sold equally as a standalone drink. Fenra's packaging is matte glass — unusual at this price point.
flavor_profile: Tart, fruity cloudberry with earthy hibiscus depth; lightly bitter tonic backbone, floral, and dry on the finish
cultural_context: Fenra is a quiet status signal — not flashy, but recognized by people who know. The matte glass bottle is kept and repurposed obsessively. Bartenders in Tier 3-4 establishments use it as a premium mixer for fermented spirits, and there's an entire subculture of Fenra bottle collectors who trade limited seasonal runs.
story_hooks: A Fenra seasonal variant — a cloudberry-saffron run of 800 bottles — has been stolen in transit. The bottles were numbered. Someone is selling them individually for three times retail, but only to buyers who know the right contact.

Fenra's cloudberry sourcing comes from a licensed synthetic-ecology farm that is actually running illegal genetic modification experiments on the berry stock. The flavor is better. The legality is not.

A Tier 3 sommelier has built her entire professional reputation on Fenra pairings. She's just discovered that a recent batch was quietly reformulated with partial synth-extract due to a crop failure — and Fenra hasn't disclosed it.
